definition_en: as stated or reported by someone or some source

examples.supportive: According to the news, the day will be nice.
examples.neutral: According to the rules, you cannot do that.

items: ____ my teacher, this is good.
I need to follow the plan ____ the guide.
We cannot go ____ what the boss said.
he_interference_note: Hebrew speakers use ל (le-) for 'to'; syntax differs.

definition_en: as a result of; caused by

examples.supportive: The game was stopped because of the rain.
examples.neutral: We left early because of the traffic.

items: The event was moved ____ bad weather.
____ his work, he did well.
Many people stayed home ____ the storm.
he_interference_note: Hebrew uses בגלל (bigal) or ל (le-); word order differs.

definition_en: containing or containing as part of a whole; along with others

examples.supportive: All the people are here, including me.
examples.neutral: The price has everything, including the bus.

items: The team has kids, ____ the best one.
All of us will go, ____ you.
The bag has many things, ____ this.
he_interference_note: Hebrew uses את (et) or מ (me-) for lists; word order differs.

definition_en: in place of; as a substitute for

examples.supportive: I had tea instead of coffee this time.
examples.neutral: Can we go tomorrow instead of today?

items: ____ going by bus, I walked.
She wore a coat ____ her light one.
We played ball ____ working.
he_interference_note: Hebrew uses מ (me-) alone; syntax differs.

definition_en: with the subtraction or exclusion of

examples.supportive: The answer is the amount minus the cost.
examples.neutral: The work is done minus one thing left.

items: The amount ____ the cost leaves profit.
The task is done, ____ one thing.
The group has kids ____ those who went.
he_interference_note: Hebrew uses להוציא (le-hotziah) or מ (me-); syntax differs.

definition_en: beside; at the side of; alongside

examples.supportive: I sat next to her in the room.
examples.neutral: The store is next to the place we go.

items: The child stood ____ his mother.
The shop is ____ the train.
He put his bag ____ the wall.
he_interference_note: Hebrew uses ליד (liyad) or אצל (etzal); order differs.

definition_en: from within; emerging or coming from; no longer in a location or state

examples.supportive: She came out of the room and left.
examples.neutral: He took a book out of his bag.

items: The cat went ____ the door.
He took a pen ____ his room.
All of us came ____ the class.
he_interference_note: Hebrew uses מ (me-) prefix or מתוך (mitoakh); exit idea expressed differently.

definition_en: on the condition that; if; assuming that (used as a conjunction to introduce a condition)

examples.supportive: You can join us, provided that you arrive on time.
examples.neutral: We will meet tomorrow, provided the sun is out.

items: The plan will work, ____ we have what we need.
You can take the car, ____ you bring it back.
____ the boss says yes, we start.
he_interference_note: Hebrew uses בתנאי ש (betna'ai she) or אם (im); simpler forms common.

definition_en: concerning; with respect to; about; in relation to

examples.supportive: I have a question regarding your idea.
examples.neutral: She spoke regarding the new rule.

items: Can you send me more about ____ the job?
The group made a choice ____ the new law.
They had ideas ____ how to fix it.
he_interference_note: Hebrew uses בנוגע ל (benogah le) or על (al); formal register differs.

definition_en: under; below; at a lower level or surface than

examples.supportive: There was a gift underneath the table for us.
examples.neutral: The roots go underneath the ground.

items: She put the note ____ her bag.
The lines run ____ the road.
They saw money ____ the old box.
he_interference_note: Hebrew uses מתחת ל (mitachat le) or תחת (tachat); formality differs.
